Imagine… AI becomes smarter than every human on Earth.
What would happen to us?
You ask it a question.
It answers before you finish typing.
Then.
It starts improving itself.
In 1997, a computer beat the world chess champion.
In 2016, AlphaGo won with a move no human expert expected.
Then it predicted the shapes of two hundred million proteins.
A mind like that could out-think all of us.
And we might not understand its choices.
Your brain has eighty-six billion neurons… and runs on just twenty watts.
Today's AI needs entire data centers.
But here's the twist.
You have been watching AI this whole time.
This voice.
These images.
None of it is human.
So remember.
In 1965, a mathematician warned: a super-intelligent machine could be the last invention we ever need.
